m.s: Heat the oven to 200°C. You'll need {chk_whole}, which is one bird for every 4 serves. Pat dry, then rub all over with softened {butter}, crushed {garlic} and plenty of salt. Tuck {lemon}, cut into wedges, inside the bird.
Roast for about 1 hour 20 minutes for a 1.8kg bird, until the skin is golden and the juices run clear when you pierce the thigh (75°C in the thickest part).

Cut {potato} into chunks and boil in salted water for 8 minutes. Drain, then shake in the pot to rough up the edges. Tip onto an oiled tray with {carrot} in chunks, season and roast alongside the chook for 50 minutes, turning once.
Rest the chook on a board for 10 minutes, loosely covered. Steam or boil {greenbeans} for 3 minutes until bright green.

Pour the pan juices into a small saucepan and skim off most of the fat. Add {stockpowder} dissolved in 1 cup hot water and bring to a simmer. Mix {cornflour} with a splash of cold water, whisk it in and simmer for 2 minutes until thick and glossy. Season to taste.
Carve the chook and serve with the potatoes, carrots, beans and gravy.

l: Strip the leftover meat and pack it with potatoes and greens, with spare gravy in a little container. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: Use 100% maize cornflour and check the stock powder. Naturally GF otherwise.
